scenes.line2: Why do they trip up devs?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why deadlocks and starvation are such common interview traps in Go concurrency?

scenes.label: Deadlock
scenes.sub: Goroutines wait forever—no one can proceed.
scenes.say: A deadlock happens when goroutines wait on each other forever. No one moves forward.

scenes.code:
ch := make(chan int)
ch <- 1 // Deadlock: no receiver
scenes.say: Here, sending to a channel with no receiver causes an instant deadlock.

scenes.label: Starvation
scenes.sub: Some goroutines never get resources or scheduled.
scenes.say: Starvation is when some goroutines never get scheduled or can't access resources.

rows.b: Make sure every send has a receive
Always acquire locks in same order

scenes.say: To avoid both issues, always check all code paths, lock in the same order, and unlock with defer.

scenes.question: How do you avoid mutex deadlocks?
scenes.right: Always lock in a consistent order and use defer to unlock.
scenes.say: Interview trap: How do you avoid mutex deadlocks? Don't just release locks manually. Always lock in the same order and use defer to unlock.
